_about: Entomology for the Hatching now section, one entry per food in foods.json: kind (mayfly, caddis, stonefly, midge, terrestrial, other insect, crustacean, baitfish or other), scientific name, the stages fish take, time of day, and a one-line tip. A first draft from common angling references, not yet checked against a cited source for each food; the PRD asks Edward to review every entry before launch.

midge.time_of_day: All day; midday is best in winter
midge.tip: Hang a Zebra Midge under an indicator; switch to a Griffith's Gnat when adults cluster.

chironomid.tip: Suspend a chironomid pupa just off the bottom under an indicator and let it sit.

bwo.time_of_day: Midday to mid-afternoon, best on cool, overcast or drizzly days
bwo.tip: Drift a small nymph before the hatch, then switch to an emerger.

pmd.tip: Nymph the riffles until fish rise, then fish a cripple or sparkle dun.

hendrickson.time_of_day: Early to mid-afternoon; spinners fall at dusk
hendrickson.tip: Swing a soft hackle as the nymphs rise, then fish a Red Quill to rising fish.

sulfur.tip: Fish an emerger in the last hour of light; spinners fall at dark.

march_brown.tip: Duns trickle off all day, so a March Brown dry can work without a heavy hatch.

green_drake.time_of_day: Evening in the East; midday in the West
green_drake.tip: Big fish rise to drakes; in the East, fish the coffin fly spinner after dark.

trico.tip: Fish a size 22 to 24 spinner on long, fine tippet once the spinners hit the water.

callibaetis.tip: Strip a small nymph by weed beds, then lead cruising fish with a parachute.

caddis.tip: Swing a pupa or soft hackle during the emergence, then skate an Elk Hair Caddis at dusk.

october_caddis.tip: Skate a big orange caddis in the evening; drift a cased-caddis nymph by day.

salmonfly.time_of_day: Midday to afternoon, when the adults fly
salmonfly.tip: Pound a big foam dry against the banks; before the hatch, bounce a stonefly nymph.

golden_stone.tip: Fish a golden stone dry along the banks with a stonefly nymph dropper.

yellow_sally.tip: Drop a small yellow Stimulator along riffle edges late in the day.

stonefly_nymph.time_of_day: Any time; best in high or rising water
stonefly_nymph.tip: Bounce a heavy stonefly nymph through fast, rocky runs as the anchor fly.

hopper.tip: Slap a hopper tight to grassy banks, with a nymph dropper under it.

ant.time_of_day: Midday to afternoon; flying-ant falls in late summer
ant.tip: Fish a small foam ant in the film along shaded banks.

beetle.tip: Plop a foam beetle under overhanging trees; the splash draws the take.

scud.tip: Dead-drift a scud near the bottom through weedy runs.

sowbug.tip: Drift a gray sowbug along the bottom of weedy riffles.

worm.time_of_day: Any time; best in high, rising or dirty water
worm.tip: Add a San Juan Worm when flows rise or the water colors up.

egg.tip: Drift a small egg below spawning fish, and leave fish on their redds alone.

leech.tip: Strip a leech slowly with long pauses so the tail keeps moving.

sculpin.time_of_day: Dawn, dusk, overcast days and high water
sculpin.tip: Keep a sculpin on the bottom with a sinking line and short, erratic strips.

baitfish_fw.time_of_day: Low light, and high or off-color water
baitfish_fw.tip: Swing or strip a minnow streamer past structure; go small when fry are out.

crayfish.time_of_day: Evening and night, or all day in stained water
crayfish.tip: Hop a crayfish backward along rocky bottoms, the way they flee.

damsel.tip: Strip a slim olive nymph slowly toward shore, just under the surface.

dragonfly_nymph.tip: Crawl a dragonfly nymph along the bottom with short strips and long pauses.

cranefly.time_of_day: Larvae after rain; adults on fall afternoons
cranefly.tip: Drift a crane fly larva when rising water washes them out of the banks.

mouse.tip: Swim a mouse slowly across the current on dark nights, and wait for the weight before setting.

frog.tip: Work a frog along lily pads and grass lines, pausing between pops.

topwater_bug.latin: Cicadas, moths and other big insects
topwater_bug.tip: Pop a bug near cover, then let it sit until the rings fade.

baitfish_warm.latin: Shad, shiners and sunfish fry (Dorosoma, Notropis, Lepomis)
baitfish_warm.time_of_day: Dawn and dusk; all day in stained water
baitfish_warm.tip: Strip a baitfish streamer past points and drop-offs, matched to the forage's size.

hellgrammite.tip: Dead-drift or crawl a hellgrammite through riffles and along rocky bottoms.

shrimp.time_of_day: Rising tides; midday light for sight fishing
shrimp.tip: Lead a tailing fish by a few feet and strip in short, slow bumps.

crab.latin: Callinectes, Xanthidae and Uca (blue, mud and fiddler crabs)
crab.tip: Land a crab just ahead of the fish and let it sink; strip only if it follows.

sand_eel.time_of_day: Dawn, dusk and night, on moving tides
sand_eel.tip: Swing a slim sand eel fly across the current as the tide moves.

baitfish_salt.latin: Menhaden, mullet, silversides and anchovies (Brevoortia, Mugil, Menidia, Anchoa)
baitfish_salt.time_of_day: Dawn and dusk, when bait is pushed to the top
baitfish_salt.tip: Find birds working bait and strip a matching streamer fast.

squid.tip: Strip a squid fly in long, darting pulls along rips and jetties.

worm_hatch.tip: Twitch a small red-and-black worm fly through swirling fish at dusk.

isonychia.time_of_day: Evening; nymphs crawl out on midstream rocks
isonychia.tip: Strip a dark swimming nymph through fast riffles; fish a slate drake dry at dusk.

shad.time_of_day: During generation and after cold snaps
shad.tip: Dead-drift or twitch a white shad pattern below the dam when stunned shad come through.

smelt.time_of_day: Dawn, dusk and overcast days during the runs
smelt.tip: Strip a slim smelt streamer such as a Grey Ghost near inlets and outlets after ice-out.
